title: A second, older streak rule (days in a row) still feeds the coach and the gym summary
what: The app decided there is one streak: weeks in a row with a workout. The home summary data still also works out an older streak in days (two rest days break it). The coach's streak answer and the summary row sent to the gym use the days number, so a member who sees '5 weeks in a row' can be told 'You're on a 3-day training streak' or 'no active streak'.
expected: Every place that speaks of a streak uses the one weeks-in-a-row rule, and the old days rule is removed.
who: members (when the coach is on) and gyms reading the member summary
how_often: every time the coach is asked about a streak or the summary is sent
fix_line: Drop the days streak and give the coach and the summary the weeks streak

title: The recovery score is worked out twice with two different muscle rules, and its scoring has no test of its own
what: The old home summary works out a recovery score with one rule for which muscles were worked, then a newer step works it out again with a different rule (it counts planks and pull-ups) and replaces it, except when the recent workouts were not handed in, when the old score is kept. The scoring itself (start at 75, the bands for primed, good, moderate, low) is never checked by a test; the only test that runs it compares the function with itself.
expected: One recovery calculation with one muscle rule, and a test that checks the score and label for known workouts.
who: members once the recovery card is shown again
fix_line: Keep only the newer recovery step and add a test of its score bands

title: The MettleUp Plus wiring and the shared screen-loading helpers have no test at all
what: The step that starts the free month, follows the gym's Plus switch, locks the watch and asks Google Play what was bought has no test. Nor do the free-month pop-ups, the Plus page link gate and the locked-feature message. The shared helpers every data screen uses to load, read again after a failure, and guard Back are also never loaded by a test. Several money bugs were already found in this Plus wiring.
expected: Each of these has at least one test that checks what it does before Plus is switched on.
who: members, once Plus is switched on
fix_line: Add small tests for the Plus start-up step, its pop-ups and the shared loading helpers

title: Two tests promise a behaviour but only look for words in the code
what: A test named 'a failed answer is asked again after 30 minutes' never waits or asks again; it only checks that two bits of text appear in the code. A test that the team-reply notification rings only checks the code's text too. Both stay green if the behaviour breaks in a way that keeps the words.
expected: Each test runs the code with a stand-in clock or stand-in notification and checks the result.
fix_line: Rewrite the two tests to run the code and check what it does
